messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — after rolling v4.0 to canary we saw a sharp p95/p99 latency tail and throughput drop on a subset of hosts, starting ~07:10 UTC. infra-bot alerted.

infra-bot: ALERT: cluster/serving-pool-7 p99 latency jumped from 60ms -> 420ms at 07:12 UTC. Error rate stable.

Maya Patel: This correlates with tokenizer changes in v4.0 (byte-unicode mapping + different split rules). Not all tenants affected — mostly medium-RT burst tenants.

Leo Chan: I profiled one of the affected workers. Flame shows a hot path in kernel selection and small-batch dispatch overhead. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% on those hosts.

Ashley Ramos: Interesting — if tokenizer now emits more short sub-tokens (common for emojis / punctuation tweaks) that can change seq-len distribution. Our batcher heuristics bucket by tokens and time window; more short sequences can produce lots of tiny batches.

Sriram Iyer: Confirmed. seq-len histogram from canary traces: before v4.0 median=64, after canary median=18, but tail still 512. That shifts the batcher into many <8-token batches. Batcher timeout = 5ms so we have lots of micro-batches.

Maya Patel: Can you paste profiler snapshot and p99 numbers?

Leo Chan: Paste of quick perf dump:

```
p99: 420ms (worker A)
p95: 190ms
throughput: -23% overall on pool-7
profiler top:
  - kernel_selector: 34%
  - batcher.dispatch_small: 22%
  - kv_cache.lookup: 12% (miss rate up)
  - attn_kernels_short_seq_path: 8%
```

Ashley Ramos: The runtime has a fastpath kernel optimized for long sequences and a separate short-seq kernel. It looks like our heuristic picked the slower short-seq kernel due to changed tokenization, but the short-seq kernel isn't optimized for many tiny batches — kernel launch overhead dominates.

Sriram Iyer: Also KV cache prefix normalization: the tokenizer changes slightly altered prefix boundaries so stored cache keys don't align -> more cold cache lookups. That explains the KV miss increase.

Maya Patel: Good catch. Two orthogonal causes: micro-batching (batcher heuristic + timeout) and KV cache misalignment. We should mitigate quickly. Options: rollback v4.0, tweak batcher timeout/bucketing, or force kernel override to stable variant.

Leo Chan: Quick mitigation plan I exercised on canary host: increase batching window from 5ms -> 12ms and force kernel override to "stable-int8" for the short path. After change p99 dropped from 420 -> 110ms and throughput recovered ~+15%. KV misses still elevated though.

Ashley Ramos: For KV cache: we can add a canonicalization step in the tokenizer shim to preserve old prefix behavior (normalize prefix bytes) as a short-term compatibility layer. That should restore high KV hit rate.

Sriram Iyer: TL;DR hotfix rollout: (1) Apply kernel override on canary + bump batcher window; (2) deploy tokenizer shim that normalizes prefixes; (3) run A/B to validate quality impact. If quality OK, roll to production.

Maya Patel: Agreed. I'll open a rollback if hotfix doesn't show improvement in 30m. Leo, can you run an A/B on 10% of traffic with hotfix? Also collect sample prompts for evaluation.

Leo Chan: Starting A/B now. Command I'm using to patch canary pool: `infractl apply -f hotfix-batcher-kernel.yml --pool=serving-pool-7 --patch`. Will stream logs.

deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix-batcher-kernel.yml -> serving-pool-7 (10% traffic). Job id: dpl-2026-04-11-87.

infra-bot: metrics update 07:40 UTC: canary hotfix p99=108ms, throughput +12%, kv_miss_rate reduced from 18% -> 9% after tokenizer shim applied to canary.

Maya Patel: Nice. Keep monitoring for quality regressions (diff evaluation set). If eval OK after 1h, schedule staged rollout.

Ashley Ramos: I'll run a quick diff on tokenization and model logits. If tokenizer shim changes logits significantly we'll need more careful rollout. Expecting minimal change — shim only normalizes prefixes.

Sriram Iyer: Followup actions: update batcher to use seq-length-aware batching (prefer bucketing by normalized token spans), add telemetry for tokenization delta metrics, and add a kernel-selection failsafe to avoid launching the short-seq kernel when micro-batch rate > X per second. Filing GH issues.

Maya Patel: Thanks team. Filing incident summary and postmortem checklist. Will include root cause notes and the temporary fixes we used. :white_check_mark:
